blocks.orig: Tanzania is much bigger than many travellers imagine. With enormous national parks, remote safari regions, and long travel routes between destinations, understanding realistic travel times is key to creating a balanced safari itinerary.
blocks.html: Many travellers underestimate just how large Tanzania is. The national parks are vast, some safari areas are remote and the routes linking destinations are long, so knowing what travel times are realistic is essential for building a well-balanced safari itinerary.

blocks.orig: Why 100 km at home doesn’t equal 100 km on safari
blocks.html: Why a 100 km drive on safari is not the same as 100 km back home

blocks.orig: Driving in Tanzania is very different from driving on highways in Europe or the US. Distances between national parks may seem manageable on a map, but travel often takes longer than expected. Road conditions can vary greatly, especially outside major cities. Traffic, police checkpoints, changing weather conditions and long stretches through remote safari regions can all affect travel times. And because journeys between parks often cover huge areas of wilderness, safaris are planned in hours rather than kilometres.
blocks.html: Getting around Tanzania by road is nothing like driving on a European or American motorway. On a map, the distance from one national park to the next can look easy, yet the journey frequently lasts longer than you would expect. Outside the larger cities, road surfaces differ enormously. Travel times can be influenced by traffic, police checks, shifting weather and long sections through isolated safari country. Since the drives between parks often cross wide stretches of wilderness, we plan safaris in hours instead of kilometres.

blocks.orig: More time in nature, less time on the road
blocks.html: Spend more time in nature and less on the road

blocks.orig: Some safari itineraries may look great on paper, offering a different destination every day. In reality, these rushed itineraries often mean leaving the parks early and spending more time on the road than in nature.
blocks.html: On paper, a safari itinerary with a new destination every single day can look appealing. In practice, such hurried schedules usually mean you leave the parks early and spend more hours driving than out in nature.

blocks.orig: We design our safaris differently. By carefully balancing travel times, overnight stays and game drives, we create journeys with more time in nature and less time on the road.
blocks.html: Our approach to safaris is different. We weigh up travel times, overnight stops and game drives with care, so your journey gives you more time in nature and less time on the road.

blocks.orig: Tourists are not allowed on the road outside cities after dark, so airport transfers need to be timed carefully. If your first or last night is in the city, there is no problem – we can pick you up and drop you off day and night.
blocks.html: After dark, tourists may not travel on roads outside the cities, which is why airport transfers have to be planned with care. When your first or last night is spent in the city, this is not an issue – we can collect you and drop you off at any hour.

blocks.orig: But if you’re heading straight to or from a national park, your flight should arrive before 1:00 PM or depart after 1:00 PM. This applies to Arusha, Kilimanjaro International and Julius Nyerere International airports.
blocks.html: If you are travelling directly to or from a national park, however, your flight needs to land before 1:00 PM or take off after 1:00 PM. This rule covers Arusha, Kilimanjaro International and Julius Nyerere International airports.
